entries.test: Public neocloud customer contracts, revenue concentration disclosures and capital spending would show whether customers outside the stated exceptions support the scale of investment.
entries.note: The preceding sentence supports the exclusion of business originating with OpenAI and Anthropic.

entries.test: Utilization and customer spending records for the capacity under construction would show whether it becomes fully used without either stated condition occurring.
entries.note: The claim sets necessary conditions for full utilization without a calendar deadline.
“I’d wager” hedges the numerical share, although the broader dependency is asserted firmly.

entries.test: Company growth forecasts, customer concentration disclosures and AI-lab financing and spending records would establish how the projected growth depends on these two customers.
entries.note: This asserts an existing dependency underlying future growth trajectories.

entries.test: AI-compute customer spending and the labs’ financial results would show whether demand is concentrated in them and whether they become able to sustain that spending.
entries.note: The surrounding discussion concerns AI compute demand; “AI demand” broadens the proposition to the whole AI market.
Neither “super fast” nor the outcome for which growth is sufficient supplies a shared test in this standalone claim.

entries.test: Public capacity inventories, construction budgets and contracted compute requirements would show whether fulfilling the revenue-generating contracts requires additional capital investment.
entries.note: “All this money” refers to the revenues from the discussed compute commitments.
“Catastrophic failure” evaluates the revenue figure rather than supplying a factual threshold.
“Suggests” presents the demand conclusion as a tentative inference.

entries.test: Comparable public revenue and customer spending data would show whether another vendor has substantial AI demand despite Microsoft's asserted lack of it.
entries.note: The condition concerns the current market, so it is not a conditional forecast.
Revenue performance is testable, but the full claim attributes an unobservable motive to everyone avoiding the subject.
He evaluates a quoted expectation for the following quarter; the proposition converts it into a realized contribution. “Pathetic” remains a value judgment.

entries.test: Documented workplace sanctions or career penalties explicitly tied to refusing to claim large AI productivity gains would test the predicted professional consequences.
entries.note: He credits Suresh while adopting the assertion in his own voice.
This explicitly prescribes shame and exclusion.
“A series of exploits used to mask” does not identify a sufficiently definite mechanism or outcome for a shared test.
The forecast is explicitly qualified by “likely,” “if anything” and “perhaps.” The separate assertion that no money has been raised is testable.
The claim combines a counterfactual about financing necessity with an assertion of the deals’ exclusive purpose.

entries.test: Hyperscaler cash-flow statements, capital budgets, financing disclosures and AI revenue and cost data would show whether cash flows are deteriorating and additional capex depends on debt.
entries.note: In context, negative cash flows refer to cash remaining after capital expenditure.

entries.test: Meta's public AI strategy, compute spending, AI revenue disclosures and measured advertising results would test the assertions about its spending, strategy, revenues and ad benefits.
entries.note: The context supports reading “meaningful revenues” as AI revenues.

entries.test: Public capacity plans, compute pricing and utilization assumptions, customer spending totals and lab financing records would test the capacity economics, demand estimate and funding concentration.
entries.note: “Best-case scenario” presents an asserted upper bound, not a probability hedge.

entries.test: If the labs cannot sustain the stated compute spending, subsequent hyperscaler revenue growth and the named infrastructure companies’ financial distress would test the predicted consequences.
entries.note: “Apocalyptic circumstances” has a plain contextual reading of severe financial distress, although no precise threshold is supplied.

entries.test: Public acquisition offers, completed sales, IPO filings and listing activity for venture-backed AI companies would test the asserted scarcity of exit prospects.
entries.note: “Needs a miracle” is rhetorical emphasis; the stated lack of evidence for exits is a testable observation.
